title.gateDoubled: ReaGate's Dry is at {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB with Wet open, so your voice goes through it twice and jumps about 6 dB louder whenever the gate opens. Set Dry to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
title.tooLoud: Your voice is too loud and can distort: bring the compressor's Wet down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so your speech sits around {{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS.
title.tooQuiet: Your voice is too quiet: bring the compressor's Wet up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so your speech gets closer to {{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS.

deadSilence.noiseRemoval: Your pauses drop to dead silence, so the noise removal is cutting into your voice: turn its strength down a step. Pauses should sound quiet, not dead.
deadSilence.gate: Your pauses drop to dead silence, so the gate is closing on your voice: lower its Threshold {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so it opens earlier. Pauses should sound quiet, not dead.

title.noisyPause: Your pauses still carry background noise and you want it gone: turn the noise removal's strength up a step.

high.boom: Too much boom: lower the 150 Hz low shelf by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.warmth: Your voice sounds thick: lower the 250 Hz band by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.mud: Your voice sounds muddy or boxy: lower the 450 Hz band by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.presence: Your voice sounds harsh: lower the 3.5 kHz band by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.sibilance: Your S sounds are sharp: lower the 10 kHz high shelf by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

low.boom: Your voice lacks bass: raise the 150 Hz low shelf by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.warmth: Your voice sounds thin: raise the 250 Hz band by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.mud: Your voice sounds hollow: raise the 450 Hz band by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.presence: Your voice sounds dull or far away: raise the 3.5 kHz band by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.sibilance: Your voice lacks crispness: raise the 10 kHz high shelf by {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

advice.undo: Put it back the way it was.
advice.conflict: That value was changed after you applied this, so Undo would overwrite your change. Set it back with its slider instead.
advice.missing: That effect or value isn't in the chain any more.

reaplugs.highpass: In ReaEQ, enable a band, set Type to High Pass, and enter the frequency.
reaplugs.eqCut: In ReaEQ, enable a free band, set Type to Band, enter the frequency and a negative gain.
reaplugs.eqBoost: In ReaEQ, enable a free band, set Type to Band, enter the frequency and a positive gain.
reaplugs.lowShelf: In ReaEQ, enable Band 1, set Type to Low Shelf, enter the frequency and gain.
reaplugs.highShelf: In ReaEQ, enable the last band, set Type to High Shelf, enter the frequency and gain.
reaplugs.noiseSubtract: In ReaFIR, set Mode to Subtract and build a noise profile from a quiet section.
reaplugs.gate: In ReaGate, enable the plugin and set the Threshold so it closes in pauses but stays open on your voice.
reaplugs.compress: In ReaComp, enable the plugin and set Threshold and Ratio to even out your level.
reaplugs.deess: Enable the De-Esser plugin to tame sharp S sounds.

equalizerApo.openConfig: Open Equalizer APO's Configuration Editor (or edit config.ini directly).
equalizerApo.save: Save the configuration. Changes take effect immediately on all audio.
equalizerApo.unsupported: Equalizer APO does not support this type of fix. Use Wave Link ReaPlugs instead.

level.up: Your voice was quiet ({{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS): the compressor's Wet, its make-up gain, goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so your speech sits near {{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS.
level.down: Your voice was too loud ({{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS): the compressor's Wet comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so your speech sits near {{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS.
level.peaks: Your loudest moments were too close to clipping (peak {{peak, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS): the compressor's Wet comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB to leave room.
level.gateFollows: ReaGate comes after the compressor: its Threshold moves {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB with the Wet, so the gate still closes in the pauses and stays open on your words.

trim.up: The other changes left your voice at {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS: the compressor's Wet goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so your speech is back near {{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS.
trim.down: The other changes left your voice at {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS: the compressor's Wet comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so your speech is back near {{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS.

reason.gateDoubled: ReaGate's Dry was at {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB with Wet open, so your voice passed twice and the pauses were not reduced: Dry goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

dead.gateDry: The gate cut your pauses to dead silence: its Dry goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, so pauses stay quiet instead of dead.
dead.strength: The noise removal was cutting into your voice or leaving dead silence in the pauses: its strength comes down.
dead.threshold: The gate was closing on your quiet words: its Threshold goes {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB lower so it opens earlier.

noise.strength: Your pauses carried room noise (your voice was only {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above it): the noise removal gets stronger.
noise.threshold: The gate stayed open between your words: its Threshold goes up to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so it closes in the pauses.
noise.onStrength: Noise Removal starts at strength {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}: the lightest setting that brought the room down without cutting into your voice.

high.boom: Too much boom (80–160 Hz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.warmth: Your voice sounded thick (160–320 Hz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.mud: Your voice sounded muddy or boxy (320–640 Hz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.body: Your voice sounded honky (640 Hz–1.25 kHz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.definition: Your voice sounded nasal (1.25–2.5 kHz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.presence: Your voice sounded harsh (2.5–5 kHz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.sibilance: Your S sounds were sharp (5–10 kHz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
high.air: Too much hiss on top (10–16 kHz): this EQ band comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

low.boom: Your voice lacked bass (80–160 Hz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.warmth: Your voice sounded thin (160–320 Hz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.mud: Your voice sounded hollow (320–640 Hz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.body: Your voice lacked body (640 Hz–1.25 kHz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.definition: Your voice lacked definition (1.25–2.5 kHz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.presence: Your voice sounded dull or far away (2.5–5 kHz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.sibilance: Your voice lacked crispness (5–10 kHz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
low.air: Your voice lacked air (10–16 kHz): this EQ band goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

shape.high: Too much {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz in your voice: this EQ band is moved onto it and made as wide as the problem, so the cut lands there and not on the healthy parts next to it.
shape.low: Too little {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz in your voice: this EQ band is moved onto it and made as wide as the gap, so the lift lands where your voice is missing it.

comp.ratio: Your volume swung {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB between loud and quiet moments: the compressor's Ratio goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}:1 so it evens them out more.
comp.threshold: Your volume swung {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB between loud and quiet moments: the compressor's Threshold goes down to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so it starts working earlier.

switch.reafirDamage: ReaFIR was removing parts of your voice along with the noise (words cut off or dropped to silence): it is switched off. The test run without it measured your voice whole again.
switch.reafirTone: ReaFIR was changing the tone of your voice, not only the noise ({{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz was out of balance): it is switched off, and the test run without it measured closer to your target.
switch.nrOn: Your pauses still carried room noise (your voice was only {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above it) and Elgato Noise Removal was sitting in your chain switched off: it is switched on.

words.times: The gate was closing on the ends of your words: its Hold and Release get longer, so it stays open until a word is over.
words.threshold: The gate was cutting the starts of your quiet words: its Threshold goes down to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, safely under them, so it opens in time.
words.floor: The gate was still cutting into quiet words: its Dry goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, so what it turns down stays audible instead of being cut.
words.strength: Noise Removal was taking the soft starts or ends of words along with the room: its strength goes down to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}, so they come through whole.
words.gateOff: You hear words cut off, and Noise Removal already keeps your pauses silent: ReaGate now lets everything through, so it can no longer cut the start or end of a word.

peak.attack: Short spikes at the start of your words were getting through before the compressor reacted, and the make-up gain made them distort: its Attack goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} ms so it catches them.
peak.comp: Your loudest moments were far above the rest of your voice and distorted: the compressor's Threshold goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB and its Ratio up, so it holds them back.
peak.strength: Words starting out of complete silence made spikes that distorted: the noise removal's strength goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} so the pauses are not cut to nothing.

bursts.gate: Noise Removal let the room through for a moment in your pauses (it reacts to how much room it receives): ReaGate, which comes before it, now closes in the pauses, so Noise Removal gets less room and stays silent.
bursts.level: The compressor's Wet goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB to give your voice back what the gate took, so it stays as loud as it was.
bursts.strength: Noise Removal still let the room through for a moment in some pauses: its strength goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}, and the test run cut no word.

metallic.strength: You hear your voice as metallic or robotic, which is what a strong Noise Removal does: its strength comes down to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}.

flat.ratio: Your voice sounded flat (its loud and quiet moments only {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB apart): the compressor's Ratio comes down to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}:1 so it squeezes less.
flat.threshold: Your voice sounded flat (its loud and quiet moments only {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB apart): the compressor's Threshold goes up to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB so it works on fewer moments.

hum.cut: A hum at {{hz, number}} Hz sat in your room noise: a free EQ band goes onto it, narrow, {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB down.

hiss.shelf: A high hiss sat in your pauses: the EQ's top shelf comes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, where the room is louder than your voice.

unmet.notEnoughSpeech: There isn't enough speech in this recording to tune on. Record again: stay quiet for 3 seconds, then talk for about 20.
unmet.silent: Nothing of your voice comes out of the chain: an effect is cutting everything. Switch effects off one at a time to find it, then run this again.
unmet.clipped: The recording itself clips ({{count, number}} samples at full scale). Effects can't repair that: lower your mic gain and record again.

level.noToolQuiet: Your voice ends {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB under the target and no compressor is switched on to make it up: switch ReaComp on, or raise your mic gain.
level.noToolLoud: Your voice ends {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB over the target and no compressor is switched on to bring it down: lower your mic gain.
level.capQuiet: Your voice is still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB under the target with the compressor's Wet as high as it goes: raise your mic gain.
level.capLoud: Your voice is still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB over the target with the compressor's Wet as low as it goes: lower your mic gain.
level.peaks: Your voice is still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB under the target: any louder and your loudest moments would clip.
level.held: Your voice is still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB away from the target: moving the compressor's Wet further made the rest measure worse (an effect after it reacts to the level), so it stays here. Adjust your mic gain instead.
level.toneMoved: Bringing your voice to the target level changed its tone a little (up to {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB in one range): the noise removal after your compressor reacts to how loud your voice reaches it. Listen to the result; if the tone is off, run this again from here.

unmet.dead: Your pauses still drop to dead silence. Another effect is cutting the sound: switch effects off one at a time to find it.
unmet.chopped: Quiet words are still being cut off. Another effect is cutting the sound: switch effects off one at a time to find it.

noise.noTool: Your voice is only {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above the room noise ({{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} wanted) and nothing in your chain can reduce it: add Elgato Noise Removal, or move closer to the mic.
noise.limit: Your voice is still only {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above the room noise ({{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} wanted). More removal would cut into your voice or go past the amount you chose: move closer to the mic or quiet the room.
noise.wouldCut: Your voice is {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above the room noise ({{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} wanted). More noise reduction would start cutting your words, so the gate stays gentle: quiet the room or move closer to the mic.

tone.noEq: Your chain has no EQ switched on, so the tone can't be changed: add ReaEQ.
tone.noBand: No band in your ReaEQ reaches {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz: add a band there.
tone.sharpS: Your S sounds are still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB too strong. The EQ bands in your chain barely reach them (5–10 kHz): switch on a De-Esser, or add a ReaEQ band around 6–7 kHz.
tone.limitHigh: {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz is still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above your target. The EQ can't take more off without overdoing it or hurting other parts of your voice.
tone.limitLow: {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz is still {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB under your target. The EQ can't add more without overdoing it or lifting room noise.
tone.hidden: What you describe points at too little {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz, but that part already measures {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above your target, so it was not lifted further. What hides it is too much {{maskLo, number}}–{{maskHi, number}} Hz ({{maskDb, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB over your target): taking that down is what brings it out.
tone.alreadyHigh: What you describe points at too little {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz, but that part already measures {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above your target, so it was not lifted further. If it still sounds missing, try another sound style or a different mic position.
tone.alreadyLow: What you describe points at too much {{lo, number}}–{{hi, number}} Hz, but that part already measures {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB under your target, so it was not cut further. If it still sounds too strong, try another sound style or a different mic position.
tone.room: The EQ changes that would fix this were tested and not kept: with them your voice stood {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB less above the room noise, which costs more than the tone wins. The part of your voice that is too strong is also what carries it over the room. Quiet the room or move closer to the mic, then run this again.

spread.noComp: Your volume swings {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB between loud and quiet moments ({{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} wanted) and no compressor is switched on: switch ReaComp on.
spread.limit: Your volume still swings {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB between loud and quiet moments ({{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} wanted). More compression didn't help or would lift the room noise: keep the same distance to the mic.
spread.flat: Your voice still swings only {{spread, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB between loud and quiet moments ({{target, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} or more wanted). Less compression didn't widen it: lower the compressor's Ratio by hand, or speak with more variation.

unmet.budget: Stopped after {{renders, number}} test runs. Run it again to keep going from here.
unmet.cut: The gate still cuts the starts or ends of some words ({{pct, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} % of your speech, about {{events, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} times every 10 seconds) and making it gentler did not stop it. Switch ReaGate off, or quiet the room and run this again.

room.loud: Your room noise is loud: your voice is only {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB above it in the recording itself. Effects can hide it, but lowering it at the source helps most: move closer to the mic, turn the mic gain down, and quiet or move away from what makes the noise (fan, PC, air conditioning).

unmet.silentPauses: Your pauses now go fully silent: that is Noise Removal taking the room out, and no word is cut. If it sounds unnatural, lower its strength a little.

peak.over: Your loudest moments still reach {{peak, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS (they should stay under {{ceiling, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}}) and will distort or crackle. Nothing left in your chain can bring them down: lower your mic gain and record again.

unmet.bursts: In some pauses the room still comes through for a moment, against pauses that are otherwise silent (the loudest about {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB under your voice). None of your effects removed it without cutting words: quiet the room or move closer to the mic.
unmet.removerCut: Noise Removal takes a little of the soft starts or ends of some words along with the room ({{pct, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} % of your speech, about {{events, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} times every 10 seconds), and a lighter strength did not change that. If you hear it, quiet the room or move closer to the mic, so it has less to remove.
unmet.metallic: Noise Removal stays light (strength {{max, number}} at most) because your voice sounded metallic: some room noise comes back in your pauses. That is the trade.

hum.noBand: A hum at {{hz, number}} Hz sits in your room noise, and no ReaEQ band is free to cut it: add a narrow band at {{hz, number}} Hz, about −6 dB.

hiss.noShelf: The hiss in your pauses is louder than your voice up high, and your ReaEQ has no high shelf to take it down: add one at about 8 kHz.

change.band: {{plugin}} {{band}}: {{fromHz, number}} Hz, {{fromOct, number(maximumFractionDigits: 2)}} oct, {{fromDb, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB → {{toHz, number}} Hz, {{toOct, number(maximumFractionDigits: 2)}} oct, {{toDb, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB

ui.title: Make your mic sound better
ui.subtitle: Record your voice once, say what you want, and the app tunes your own Wave Link effects on that recording.

record.title: Record your raw mic
record.lead: About 25 seconds: stay quiet for 3 seconds so the app hears your room, then read the text out loud. Your effects aren't used here, and nothing plays back while you record.
record.quiet: Stay quiet, the app is listening to your room… {{sec, number}}
record.talk: Now read this out loud, at your usual voice and distance:
record.keepTalking: Finished the text? Keep talking about anything until the bar is full.
record.stopHint: You can stop after {{sec, number}} seconds.
record.or: Or use a recording you already have:
record.wavHint: Your raw mic without effects: 3 seconds of quiet first, then at least 10 seconds of talking.

problem.gap: Some of the audio got lost while recording (the computer was too busy), so this take has gaps. Record again.
problem.clipped: Your recording is too loud: it hits the top of the scale (clipping), and effects can't repair that. Turn your mic gain down a little and record again.
problem.quietBroken: It sounds like you talked during the first 3 seconds, so the app can't tell your room from your voice. Record again and stay quiet until the countdown ends.
problem.tooShort: This recording is too short. It needs 3 seconds of quiet and then at least 10 seconds of talking.
problem.silent: We only got silence. Pick the microphone you talk into and try again.
problem.tooQuiet: Your voice barely reached the mic. Turn up your mic gain or move closer, then record again.
problem.noisyPause: The quiet part was almost as loud as your talking. Stay silent until the countdown ends, and pause music or calls on this mic.
problem.notEnoughSpeech: There wasn't enough talking. Read the whole text after the countdown and keep going until the bar is full.
problem.notWav: This isn't a WAV file. Pick a .wav recording.
problem.format: This WAV format isn't supported. Use a mono or stereo WAV (16, 24 or 32-bit).

goals.title: What do you want?
goals.bothers: What bothers you (pick any, or none)
goals.amountHint: How far the app may move your effects from where they are now.

tuning.title: Tuning your effects
tuning.lead: The app plays your recording through your own effects, tries changes and keeps only the ones that measure better. Wave Link isn't changed.
tuning.baseline: Listening to your recording through your effects as they are now…

result.title: Listen and save

problems.title: {count, plural, one {# thing we found in your recording} other {# things we found in your recording}}

result.abHint: Switch while it plays to hear the same moment before and after.

download.noFolder: Your Downloads folder wasn't found, so the file wasn't saved.
download.writeFailed: The file couldn't be saved in your Downloads folder. Check that the disk has space and try again.

metrics.title: What changed
metrics.label: Before and after
metrics.snr: Voice over room (SNR: how far your voice stands above the room)
metrics.spread: Steadiness (difference between loud and quiet moments)
metrics.bursts: Noise bursts in pauses (the loudest, how far under your voice)

result.changes_one: {{count, number}} change, each with its reason
result.changes_other: {{count, number}} changes, each with its reason

effect.deadSilence: Measured: dead silence {{before}} → {{after}} of the recording
effect.cutSpeech: Measured: speech cut by the gate {{before}} → {{after}}
effect.burstDb: Measured: loudest noise burst in your pauses {{before}} → {{after}} under your voice
effect.removerCut: Measured: speech taken off with the room {{before}} → {{after}}

result.none: Your sound already meets these goals: nothing in your effects needs to change.
result.saved: Saved. Wave Link now uses these settings.
result.changedMeanwhile: Wave Link's settings changed after this recording was tuned, so nothing was written. Press Record again to tune from your settings as they are now.

player.noiseOnlyHelp: Plays only the moments when you are not talking: the quiet start and the pauses.

spectrum.title: Spectrum
spectrum.help: Drag a point to change the EQ: your recording is rendered again and After plays the change.
spectrum.aria: Spectrum of your recording from 20 Hz to 20 kHz: before and after, with the ReaEQ curve and its bands.
spectrum.noEq: No ReaEQ is switched on in your effects, so there is no curve to change here.
spectrum.rendering: Rendering your recording with your changes…

voiceNoise.aria: Spectrum of your recording from 20 Hz to 20 kHz: your voice and the noise when you are not talking, with the ReaEQ curve and its bands.

noise.title: In your noise
noise.caption: Measured where you are not talking: the 3 quiet seconds at the start and the pauses.

noiseCut.help: Takes the noise measured here out: steady whistles with narrow EQ cuts, and the rest with your noise remover, raised step by step while your voice is checked.
noiseCut.strongWarning: Strong can make the voice sound watery.

notes.noReaFir: There is no ReaFIR switched on in your effects, so the hiss was not touched.
notes.reaFirUnknown: Your ReaFIR settings are in a form this app does not know, so they were left as they are.
notes.noBand: No free ReaEQ band for the whistle at {{hz, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} Hz: set one band's gain to 0 to use it.
notes.removerLimit: Noise Removal was raised as far as your voice allows; some noise is still there.
notes.removerNoHelp: A stronger Noise Removal did not lower the noise in this recording.
notes.noNoise: This recording has no quiet stretch to measure the noise from.

tune.idle: Pick your mic and headphones, then press Start. Nothing changes in Wave Link until you save.
tune.talk: Talk normally, as if you were streaming. The numbers fill in after a second or two.

warn.monitor: Mute your mic in Wave Link's monitor mix, or you will hear yourself twice. Or set Hear to Off and listen in Wave Link.
warn.reafir: ReaFIR adds 85 ms of that in this preview.

pauses.title: Pauses
pauses.dead: Dead silence: the effects cut into your voice
pauses.noisy: You can still hear the room
pauses.none: Pause for a moment to measure

tone.title: Tone vs your goal
tone.none: Keep talking to see your tone

chart.title: Last 60 seconds
chart.aria: Speech level over the last 60 seconds, with effects and of the mic alone, the target level and a marker at each change.

spectrum.title: Live spectrum
spectrum.idle: Press Start to see the spectrum.
spectrum.noEq: Switch ReaEQ on to shape the curve here.
spectrum.aria: Spectrum of your voice from 20 Hz to 20 kHz: the mic alone and as you hear it, with the ReaEQ curve and its bands.

tones.noBand: No free ReaEQ band: set one band's gain to 0 to use it for the cut.

try.title: Try this
try.empty: Nothing to change right now. Keep talking.
try.evidence: Seen in {{sec}} s of talk, same direction every time
try.pickHear: Pick what you hear under Your sound to get EQ suggestions.

sound.title: Your sound
sound.footnote: Tone changes only for what you pick under What you hear. Level and noise advice always run.

effects.title: Your effects, in Wave Link order
effects.empty: Press Start to load your effects from Wave Link.
effects.loadFailed: Couldn't load this effect, kept as is
effects.reafirNote: ReaFIR adds 85 ms to the preview delay.

segments.title: Before and after each change
segments.empty: Start and talk: each change you make adds a row here.

calibrate.title: Calibrate noise
calibrate.lead: Leave your mic on. Stay quiet for a few seconds while the app sets your noise removal and listens to your pauses after each change, then talk normally so it can check that no word is cut. You hear every change as it happens.
calibrate.needEngine: Press Start first: the calibration listens to your mic through your effects.
calibrate.hearOff: Hear is Off. Put on your headphones and switch Hear to With effects to listen while the noise removal changes.
calibrate.settling: Waiting for the change to take effect…

do.quiet: Stay quiet: the app is listening to your room.
do.quietSet: Keep quiet: the app is setting your noise removal and listening to your pauses after each change.
do.talk: Now talk normally, as if you were streaming.
do.talkAgain: Keep talking: the noise removal was made gentler and your words are checked again.

notice.talkedQuiet: That sounded like talking, so the room measurement started over. Stay quiet until the bar is full.
notice.talkedSet: That sounded like talking while a change was being measured. It is measured again: stay quiet a little longer.
notice.noSpeech: We didn't hear you talk. Talk normally for about 10 seconds, at your usual distance from the mic.
notice.gap: Some audio got lost on the way (the computer was busy), so this part is measured again.
notice.cancelled: Calibration stopped. Your effects are back as they were.
notice.undone: Calibration undone. Your effects are back as they were.
notice.engineStopped: The audio stopped, so the calibration stopped. Press Start and calibrate again.
notice.backedOff: Some of your words were cut, so the noise removal was made gentler. Keep talking to check again.

reason.nrOn: Calibrate noise: Noise Removal was in your chain but not working, so it is switched on.
reason.strength: Calibrate noise: the lightest strength that makes your pauses silent.
reason.firOff: Calibrate noise: Noise Removal does the work now, so ReaFIR is switched off (it also took the low end of your voice).
reason.gate: Calibrate noise: the gate closes a few dB over your room, gently enough that the room doesn't pump.
reason.words: Calibrate noise: gentler, because it cut some of your words.
reason.pumping: Calibrate noise: a shallower floor, because the room went up and down between your words.
reason.more: Calibrate noise: more reduction, as you asked.
reason.less: Calibrate noise: less reduction, as you asked.
reason.back: Calibrate noise: back to how it was.

note.nothing: Your chain has nothing that removes noise (no Elgato Noise Removal or ReaGate), so there is nothing to calibrate.
note.alreadySilent: Your pauses are already silent: nothing to change.
note.notReached: Your pauses didn't go fully silent within the strength your processing amount allows. They are as quiet as it got.
note.noHelp: The noise removal didn't make your pauses quieter, so it was left as it was.
note.wouldCut: Removing the noise cut your words even at the gentlest setting, so your effects were left as they were. Words come first.
note.wordsFirst: Kept gentler so no word is cut: your pauses may not be fully silent.
note.noiseBetween: The room still comes and goes between your words (about {{db, number}} dB).
note.moreCuts: More reduction cut your words, so it went back one step.
note.morePumps: More reduction made the room go up and down between your words, so it went back one step.
note.keptReafir: Your pauses were only silent with ReaFIR on, so it stays on.
note.bursts: Now and then the room still comes through in your pauses for a moment (up to {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS).

result.cut: Some words are still cut ({{pct}} % of your voice).

tune.fileError: Wave Link's settings couldn't be read, so saving is off. {{reason}}

save.title: Save to Wave Link
save.lead: These changes go into Wave Link. A backup is made first, then Wave Link closes, the file is written, and Wave Link starts again.
save.nothing: Nothing to save: your effects are the same as in Wave Link.
save.chain: {{plugin}}: the list of effects is different
save.unsaved: {{plugin}}: changes to this effect can't be saved yet, so Wave Link keeps its own setting.
save.saving: Saving… Wave Link closes and starts again.
save.force: Wave Link didn't close by itself. Close it by force? Anything not saved in Wave Link is lost.
save.done: Saved and checked: Wave Link has your new settings.
save.unchanged: Wave Link already has these settings — nothing was written.
save.notVerified: Written, but the check after saving didn't confirm every value. Open Wave Link and look at your effects.
save.notRunning: Wave Link wasn't running; it uses these settings the next time it starts.
save.forced: Wave Link was closed by force.

restore.title: Restore backup
restore.lead: Pick the backup to put back. Wave Link closes, the backup is written over its settings, and Wave Link starts again.
restore.none: There are no backups yet. One is made every time you save to Wave Link.
restore.restoring: Restoring… Wave Link closes and starts again.
restore.restartPreview: To hear the restored settings here, press Stop and then Start.

errors.notRunning: The audio isn't running. Press Start first.
errors.noDevice: No microphone or headphones were found.
errors.deviceNotFound: The picked device isn't there any more. Pick it again.
errors.unsupportedFormat: That device can't run at 48 kHz. Pick another one or change its format in the Windows sound settings.
errors.streamFailed: The audio stopped because of a device error. Check the device and press Start again.
errors.settings: Wave Link's settings couldn't be read. Is Wave Link installed?
errors.queueFull: Too many changes at once. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.notFound: Wave Link's settings file wasn't found.
errors.parse: Wave Link's settings file couldn't be read.
errors.changedMeanwhile: Wave Link's settings changed since you pressed Start. Press Stop and Start, then save again.
errors.missingEntry: An effect to change isn't in Wave Link any more.
errors.invalidChange: Something in the change isn't valid, so nothing was written.
errors.closeTimeout: Wave Link didn't close, so nothing was written.
errors.writeFailed: The file couldn't be written. Nothing changed, and your backup is safe.
errors.startFailed: The file was written, but Wave Link didn't start again. Start it yourself.
errors.verifyFailed: The file was written, but it doesn't hold every value. Restore the backup if Wave Link sounds wrong.
